narrative:
The model estimated a 53.1% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is slightly above even odds, so the prediction is a risk flag, not a certainty, but it was enough for your application to be denied.

The denial was driven most strongly by your third-year class rank. You were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged near the sixth decile, and this was the top factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 was the next most influential factor; it is slightly above the accepted average of 3.23 and pushed toward passing. Your LSAT score of 35 was third in influence and also leaned toward passing, though it is below the accepted average of 37.18, so it did not offset the concern about your third-year standing.

To address this, ask admissions to reconsider with context explaining your third-year rank, any upward trend, and a concrete bar-preparation and academic-support plan. Consider retaking the LSAT if feasible, seek prelaw advising, and reapply after strengthening your record; you might also ask about conditional admission or support programs.
